passage:
Dear Mr. Willoughby,

My family has bought Green-Leaf organic food at your store for about five years. We buy fruit, vegetables, and eggs from this brand almost every week. We pay about 40% more than for regular food because we trust the label. I am writing to you because that trust has been broken.

Last Saturday, I bought a package of Green-Leaf organic tomatoes at your Main Street store. The label said they came from a small farm in Maple Valley. When I got home, I looked at the code on the package. It showed that the tomatoes came from a very large farm in the south. I looked it up online, and I found that this farm uses chemicals that organic farms are not allowed to use.

On Monday, I called your regional manager, Sarah Jenkins, to ask about this. She was friendly, but her answer worried me. She said that in winter, the store sometimes runs out of organic tomatoes. When this happens, regular tomatoes are put into organic packages. I do not think this is fair to customers who pay extra for organic food.

I do not want a refund or a store coupon. I want the store to be honest. Please send me a list of the farms that supply Green-Leaf products. Please also tell me when an outside inspector last checked each farm. I would also like to know how you plan to stop this from happening again.

Please reply by the end of this month. I have enjoyed shopping at your store for many years, and I hope we can solve this problem together. Until then, I will buy my vegetables at a local farmers' market.

Sincerely,
Alistair Brown
